name: Tessera Networked DMR TNDM-6 'Oracle'
description:
The TNDM-6 Oracle is Tessera's networked designated marksman rifle, extending their distributed targeting philosophy to precision engagement. When multiple Oracles are deployed, the weapons share ballistic data — wind readings from one position correct calculations at another, and target tracking data from multiple angles provides three-dimensional position estimates that no single marksman could achieve.

The Oracle fires 7mm caseless from a precision-machined barrel, and its BCI smart-scope incorporates Tessera's predictive targeting AI. The AI models target movement patterns and generates firing solutions that lead moving targets at distances where human prediction fails. When networked with other Oracles, the predictive model improves as multiple observation angles refine the target's movement vector.

Tessera sells the Oracle at Φ16,000 per unit, with squad packs of four available at Φ58,000. The networking protocol automatically distributes the most accurate ballistic data to the marksman with the best engagement angle, creating a dynamic fire-control solution that constantly optimizes which marksman should take which shot. In practice, Oracle teams achieve engagement rates that exceed the sum of their individual capabilities.
specifications:
caliber: 7mm caseless
effective_range: 900m
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic
magazine_capacity: 15 rounds
weight: 4.6 kg
tactical_use: The Oracle transforms a group of marksmen into a precision fire network. Shared ballistic data eliminates individual measurement errors, predictive targeting AI defeats evasive movement, and dynamic fire-control optimization ensures each shot is taken by the marksman with the highest probability of success. In overwatch scenarios with multiple elevated positions, an Oracle network provides interlocking precision fire that is nearly impossible to evade.
cultural_context: The Oracle represents Tessera's conviction that networking improves every military capability. Critics argue that networked marksmen lose the individual judgment and initiative that make traditional marksmen effective. Tessera responds with engagement statistics. The philosophical debate between networked collective capability and individual excellence is nowhere more sharply drawn than in the precision shooting community, where marksmanship is traditionally the most individualistic of military skills.
story_hooks: An Oracle network was hacked to inject a false target — the system displayed a phantom hostile that multiple marksmen engaged simultaneously, wasting ammunition and revealing their positions.

Two opposing forces both deployed Oracle networks. The weapons accidentally connected to each other's mesh, and for a brief moment both sides had complete visibility of the other's positions and targeting data.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular designated marksman rifle with an unmistakably networked aesthetic. The frame tapers from a robust receiver to a precision barrel, with prominent data conduits running along the left side. The overall impression is clinical and interconnected—less military hardware, more distributed intelligence made physical.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 118 cm. Barrel length: 61 cm. Width at receiver: 8 cm. The weapon has a distinctly modular profile with visible junction points where network modules interface.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but well-balanced at 4.6 kg. The weight sits forward, centered on the barrel, making shouldering natural despite the sophisticated electronics distributed throughout the frame.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-composite chassis with precision-machined steel barrel and receiver. Polymer rail systems with embedded conductive traces. Aluminum heat-sink panels along the upper receiver.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal composite with brushed steel receiver accents. The data conduits have a subtle iridescent sheen—optical fiber bundles visible beneath translucent polymer cladding.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary, with gunmetal steel highlights. Tessera's signature electric blue accent lines trace the distributed targeting network across the rail system and scope mount.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with integrated haptic feedback nodules. Slightly stippled for secure purchase even with augmented or gloved hands. The fore-grip is wrapped in soft-touch rubber with embedded temperature sensors.
distinctive_features: Dual networked scope mounts with active alignment indicators
Visible optical fiber data conduits running the length of the upper rail
Modular network interface junction boxes on either side of the receiver
Heat-sink cooling fins integrated into the rail system
Minimal iron sights—weapon relies entirely on networked smart-scope integration
Integrated antenna array disguised as rail components along the handguard
Ballistic data share indicator lights (blue LEDs) positioned on the right receiver panel
Thermal management vents sculpted into the composite furniture
Precision-machined action with minimal surface irregularities
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA corporate logo stamped into the left side of the receiver in brushed steel. 'TNDM-6 ORACLE' etched below in small caps. Network certification seal (circular, with frequency specification) positioned on the right rear of the receiver. Individual unit serial plate mounted on the magazine well in monospace font.
physical_description.condition_typical: Factory-pristine to field-worn. Oracles in active networks show minimal cosmetic damage but may have scuff marks on the data conduit cladding from rough handling. Thermal management systems often show discoloration from extended engagements. The optical surfaces are meticulously maintained—network data depends on clean sensor windows.
